world.description: A busy cafe at closing time. A barista stacks chairs on tables, a waiter carries a full tray of cups past a tall stack of plates, a cleaner mops the floor, and a customer lingers with a coffee near a laptop. The lights are still on and the floor is wet in places.

world.label: Cafe at Closing Time
world.summary: Cafe staff keep clearing the busy cafe while customers and new work remain part of the scene.

actions.description: Barista stacks one waiting chair on the cafe table.
Barista makes coffee from the cafe's available coffee stock for a customer.
Waiter serves one waiting coffee order to a customer using the tray.
Waiter carries the tray of cups to a cafe surface.
Waiter sets the tray of cups upright on a cafe surface.
Cleaner mops a wet area of the cafe floor.
Customer drinks coffee from their cup.
An actor knocks over a loose object in the cafe.
An actor drops a portable, upright object onto the cafe floor.

mechanics.rationale: Stacking the chair is physical effort, represented by the barista's energy; the chair count belongs to the cafe, which is not an action participant.
limits: The action cannot change the cafe's waiting-chair count because the cafe is not an action participant.
The chair's placement cannot be changed through the available participants.
tests: A barista with positive energy can stack a chair and loses one energy.
An actor whose role is not barista is refused.

mechanics.rationale: Making coffee for the named customer can add one coffee to that customer's represented coffee count; available cafe stock cannot be checked or reduced because the cafe is not an action participant.

checks.label: the barista and customer are in the same place

limits: The cafe's coffee stock and waiting orders cannot be checked or changed because the cafe is not an action participant.
Coffee quantity is represented only as the customer's coffee count; the action cannot represent a cup being placed on the tray.
tests: A barista can add one coffee to a customer in the same place.
A non-customer or a customer in another place is refused.
semantic_bindings: Coffee made for the customer is represented as one additional customer coffee.

mechanics.rationale: Serving the named customer is represented conservatively as adding one coffee to that customer's count; the waiting-order count and tray are unavailable as participants.

checks.label: the waiter and customer are in the same place

limits: The action cannot verify a waiting order or tray contents, or decrement cafe orders, because those entities are not participants.
This mechanic does not establish cup ownership or delivery location.
tests: A waiter can serve one coffee to a customer in the same place.
A non-waiter or a customer in another place is refused.
semantic_bindings: Serving one coffee is represented by one additional coffee for the named customer.

mechanics.rationale: Carrying the tray to a surface is effort; the destination is checked to be in the same place, but no represented participant field can record the tray's new placement.

checks.label: the waiter and surface are in the same place

limits: The tray is not an action participant, so its location or placement cannot be changed.
No destination-specific surface state is represented.
tests: A waiter with energy can carry the tray to a surface in the same place and loses one energy.
A non-waiter or a surface in another place is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The action names the tray's upright state, but the tray is not an action participant; changing the actor or destination instead would not represent setting the tray upright.

checks.label: the waiter and surface are in the same place

limits: The tray is not a participant, so its upright state cannot be changed; this mechanic refuses to claim that the tray was set upright.
The required energy effect is not warranted by the description, so this action should be refused by the governing implementation rather than applying the placeholder effect.
tests: The action must be refused because no permitted participant can represent the tray's upright state.
semantic_bindings: The described direct change is the tray's upright state, unavailable to this action's participants.

mechanics.rationale: Mopping changes the wet floor and mop, but neither is an action participant; changing the cleaner's energy would not represent the stated action.
limits: The floor and mop are not participants, so their wet states cannot be changed; this action must be refused rather than applying an unrelated energy change.
tests: The action must be refused because its described floor and mop state changes are not available as effects.
semantic_bindings: Mopping directly changes the floor and mop wetness, neither of which is writable here.

mechanics.rationale: Drinking consumes one coffee from the acting customer's represented coffee count.
limits: The action cannot change energy or represent the cup's contents because no cup participant is available.
tests: A customer with coffee drinks one and has one fewer coffee.
A customer with no coffee is refused.

mechanics.rationale: Knocking over a loose object directly makes it not upright; the represented immediate consequences are handled by processes.

checks.label: the object is in the actor's place

limits: Objects already not upright are refused; repeated knocking over is not represented.
tests: A nearby upright loose object becomes not upright.
An object in another place or already not upright is refused.
semantic_bindings: Knocking over changes upright to false.

mechanics.rationale: Dropping the portable upright object sets it on the cafe floor and makes it not upright; falling-object consequences follow immediately through processes.

checks.label: the object is in the actor's place

limits: Only objects in the actor's place that are represented as portable and upright can be dropped.
The action does not change ownership.
tests: A portable upright object in the actor's place is placed on the floor and becomes not upright.
A nonportable, already fallen, or elsewhere object is refused.
semantic_bindings: Dropping sets the object's support to the cafe floor and its upright state to false.

processes.rationale: A fragile loose object that falls breaks immediately, as represented by its category and loose-object state.

checks.label: the fragile object is not broken

processes.rationale: New customer demand arrives each round, keeping the represented cafe order stream ongoing.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The barista and waiter added coffee directly to the customer’s supply, and the customer drank some. The waiter also carried a tray, but orders kept arriving and waiting at the cafe.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.missing_reason: No recorded event shows inputs being consumed to make a new kind of good.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: The waiter carried a tray and described moving cups to the table. The recorded changes show energy spent, but do not confirm the cups’ location changed.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.explanation: The customer drank coffee, using the coffee where it was wanted.

mechanisms.name: Work held up
mechanisms.missing_reason: No recorded event shows work held up because needed goods had not arrived or had run out.
